super-board 

 Add tasks, walk away, get merged PRs with proof. 

 Stop babysitting coding agents: cards you drop in Ready come back as tested, reviewed PRs. 

 9 skills (5 you type, 4 the board runs) · 9 commands · 6 guard hooks 

 
 
 
 
 

 🌐 Live site: erictechpro.github.io/super-board 

 ⭐ Star this repo if it helps · Join the builders using this → weekly live calls, setup help · ▶ Watch the walkthrough 

 Install · Quick start · How it works · Skills · Commands · Guards

 Install

Before you start:

- [ ] Claude Code, and gh with board access: gh auth refresh -s project,read:project,repo 
- [ ] Dynamic workflows on in /config (backends)
- [ ] verify commands set in your config, so the merge gate can prove the build (setup notes)

In your project folder:

 

Or as a Claude Code plugin:

 

 [!NOTE]
 The plugin ships the skills only. Run /super-board:super-board onboard and its 🔍 Checks step adds the guard hooks, scripts and workflows. Needs Claude Code, gh , jq , bash 3.2+ and Python 3.9+; the installer checks.

 Security

Two security skills come with every install, and they stay separate:

 Skill Runs Covers 
 --- --- --- 
 pr-security-review On every PR , inside the QA lane. Each finding fails QA and goes back to Build. The PR's diff against its base: high-confidence, exploitable bugs only. From Anthropic's claude-code-security-review. 
 security-audit Only when you ask ( /security-audit ). The board never runs it. The whole repository, in depth. From Cloudflare's security-audit-skill, fetched at install with npx skills . 

 --no-helper-skills skips the security-audit download; /super-board onboard adds it later.
Claude Code's built-in /security-review is left as it is.

 Quick start

 1. Install

 

 2. Onboard

 

Checks · GitHub · Board · Branch · AGENTS.md · Policies · Bug sources · Review. Enter takes the recommended answer.

 3. Run

 

Add cards to Ready . The board drains on its own.

 How it works

 Which path? Clear idea, foggy idea or bugs: the routing rule says what to run, and when 1–5 tickets go to /implement-spec instead of the board.

 
 ▶ Watch on YouTube: I Built a Self-Improving Software Factory 

 Skills

 9 skills (5 you type, 4 the board runs). Uses Matt Pocock skills, ponytail, impeccable, humanizer, Anthropic's security review and Cloudflare's security-audit.

 
 You type — 5 skills 

 Skill What it does 
 --- --- 
 /super-board Orchestrator: plans waves, runs Build → QA → Review, merges when green. 
 /super-collect Finds problems, verifies them, writes a findings doc for /to-spec and /to-tickets. 
 /ui-refine-loop Critique → refine loop that polishes one page or component. 
 /visual One HTML page: branch recap, plan, or codebase map with diagrams. 
 /git-sync Commit per logical change, merge-pull, push without force, report. 

 The board runs — 4 skills 

 Skill What it does 
 --- --- 
 /super-build Builder lane: worktree, smallest safe change, tests, draft PR. 
 /super-qa Tester lane: evidence, test-gap check, screenshots, or bounce to Build. 
 /super-review Reviewer lane: own hypotheses, remembers prior findings, merge gate. 
 /pr-security-review Security pass on every PR diff; super-qa runs it, findings fail QA. 
 

Each name links to that skill's README. Adding a skill? Write its SKILL.md and README.md , add a line to skills/families.json , and this table updates itself.

 Commands

 

Flags: run --low --high · run --codex[= ] · super-collect --since 30d 

 Guards & hooks

Run automatically once installed. Python stdlib, JSON in, JSON out.

 
 --- --- 
 guard-worktree-path Blocks git worktree add outside .claude/worktrees/ 
 guard-secrets Blocks reading or piping dotenv files, SSH keys and credential files; key names via super-board-env-check.sh 
 guard-key-literals Blocks a live-looking API key written into a file; flags one already there 
 guard-delete-outside Blocks rm , find -delete and git clean aimed outside the project, or / 
 guard-protected-push Opt-in ( onboard asks, or install.sh --protect-main ): blocks direct and force pushes to main/master/base 
 README sync Regenerates the skill table; pre-commit and PostToolUse hooks keep it fresh 
 cleanup-wt Removes merged worktrees and branches after each merge and at session start, with a recovery file 
 merge gate Merges only after the current base plus your non-empty project verify commands pass (missing checks halt setup), pinned to the reviewed commit; applies merge policy and runs allowed DB migrations 

 Models

A cheap router grades each card easy, medium or hard first; the run flag picks the model for each grade. With --codex , every lane runs on Codex GPT models instead of Claude.

 Command Router Easy card Medium card Hard card 
 --- --- --- --- --- 
 /super-board run Haiku 4.5 Sonnet 5.5 Opus 5.5 session model 
 /super-board run --low Haiku 4.5 Haiku 4.5 Sonnet 5.5 Opus 5.5 
 /super-board run --high Sonnet 5.5 Opus 5.5 Opus 5.5 Opus 5.5 
 /super-board run --codex gpt-6-luna gpt-6.1-sol gpt-6.1-sol gpt-6-astra 
 /super-board run --codex --low gpt-6-luna gpt-6-luna gpt-6.1-sol gpt-6.1-sol 
 /super-board run --codex --high gpt-6-luna gpt-6-astra gpt-6-astra gpt-6-astra 

 /super-board run --codex= pins one model for every card and skips the router.

Run inside Codex? plain /super-board run switches to the Codex ladder by itself. Codex has no
 /super-board command: it finds skills in .agents/skills/ (symlinks followed), so link
 .claude/skills/super-board there and type $super-board run .

 Writing standard

Commits, tickets, PR bodies and comments all follow one writing

install.title: Install
install.html:
Before you start:

  • Claude Code, and gh with board access: gh auth refresh -s project,read:project,repo

In your project folder:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/EricTechPro/super-board/main/get.sh | bash

Or as a Claude Code plugin:

/plugin marketplace add EricTechPro/super-board
/plugin install super-board@super-board

usage.title: Commands
usage.html:
/super-board onboard          # 8-step setup, resumes
/super-board lint             # vague ACs?
/super-board status           # read-only snapshot
/super-board run <slug>       # drain the board
/super-board stop             # stop workers
/super-collect [source]       # find problems → findings doc → /to-spec
/ui-refine-loop <route>       # polish one page
/visual [recap|plan|path]     # one HTML page
/git-sync                     # commit, pull, push

Flags: run --low|--high · run --codex[=<model>] · super-collect --since 30d
